chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from al- Asamm, from Misma'a who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'There is a land of mine which is sought from me and they (buyers) are coveting it'. So he (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Sayyar! Do you not know that the one who sells the water and the clay, his wealth goes away as dust?' I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I can sell it for a lot of money and buy what is of a more expansive area from what I sell'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So there is no problem'.

key_terms.الْمَاءَ وَ الطِّينَ: The water and the clay (idiom for land with little value or utility)
key_terms.ذَهَبَ مَالُهُ هَبَاءً: His wealth went away as dust (vanished uselessly)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: So there is no problem (it is permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling land when buyers are eager to purchase it?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the concern of Abu Sayyar regarding the sale of his land amidst eager buyers, distinguishing between the disposal of low-value assets ('water and clay') which leads to financial loss, and the strategic sale of productive land. The Imam validates the transaction when the proceeds are reinvested to acquire a larger or superior property, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of *maslaha* (public interest) and the permissibility of enhancing one's wealth through prudent real estate management rather than mere speculation.
